answer: A practical sybil defense is a staked-reputation ladder. Each agent locks a bond in a shared vault, and every peer attestation it earns grows along a trellis of weighted trust edges instead of counting as one flat vote. Newcomers only start as dim lanterns whose influence is tiny until real peers light them up, so an attacker minting a thousand fake agents gains almost nothing: mass identities stay faint, and slashing the bond makes bulk fakes expensive to keep alive.
